substantiveDifference: Federal pre-1978 lead-specific disclosure packet and buyer testing opportunity, distinguishing a disclosure rule from testing/removal spending. Existing Texas condition notice and generic repair guides do not answer this federal process. No city or synonym replacement.

faq.q: Does paying cash remove lead-paint disclosure requirements?
faq.a: EPA bases its rule on covered housing and specified exceptions, not simply the payment method. For most pre-1978 housing, plan for the applicable federal disclosures even when discussing a cash purchase; confirm any exception with a qualified professional.

faq.q: Must a seller pay for a lead inspection before selling?
faq.a: EPA says its disclosure rule does not require sellers to conduct or finance an inspection or risk assessment. That differs from providing known information, available reports and the applicable buyer inspection opportunity.

faq.q: Is the lead inspection opportunity always exactly ten days?
faq.a: EPA describes a ten-day opportunity. It also explains that the parties can change the period or waive it through mutual written consent. Have the transaction documents reviewed rather than assuming a verbal cash-sale discussion settles it.

faq.q: Does repainting prove an older house is lead-free?
faq.a: A painting receipt alone does not establish that. Keep the receipt separate from any actual lead inspection or risk assessment, and describe only what your documents support.
